note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. On the OSA-pathway indications, this engine adjusts its raw indication-fit score by +1 when Epworth >= 11 or STOP-BANG >= 5, by -1 when neither score is recorded at all, and leaves it unchanged when a score is present but below those thresholds (as in the first persona below).

personas.name: routine-suspected-osa-home-sleep-apnoea-test-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: witnessed apnoeas, a home sleep apnoea test is the recommended (ideal) study for the suspected-osa indication; Epworth (9) and STOP-BANG (2) are both recorded but below the abnormal/high-risk thresholds, so neither the +1 evidence bonus nor the -1 no-evidence penalty applies, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate (score 8, unadjusted) + low priority + routine + accept.

request.relevantHistory: No previous sleep study. Not an occupational driver.

triage.notes: Patient can self-administer the home test with instructions provided.

personas.name: urgent-driver-assessment-home-sleep-apnoea-test-severe-sleepiness-high-priority
personas.description: HGV driver reporting severe excessive daytime sleepiness and falling asleep at the wheel: a home sleep apnoea test is the recommended (ideal) study for the driver-assessment indication, and the high Epworth (17) supports the OSA-pathway request, nudging the score from 8 to 9; the combination of occupational driving with excessive sleepiness, and the severe sleepiness alone, each independently force both urgent triage (DVLA fast-track) and high clinical priority, regardless of the routine urgency requested — expect usually-appropriate (score 9) + high priority + urgent + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: HGV driver reporting severe excessive daytime sleepiness and falling asleep at the wheel — urgent OSA assessment for a DVLA fitness-to-drive decision.
request.relevantHistory: Occupational HGV driver. Loud snoring reported by partner. Hypertension.

triage.notes: DVLA Group 2 licence; advised not to drive pending assessment per DVLA guidance.

personas.name: query-referrer-suspected-narcolepsy-other-study-mismatch-incomplete
personas.description: Excessive daytime sleepiness with cataplexy triggered by laughter: an 'other' study was requested even though multiple sleep latency testing (with preceding polysomnography also ideal) is the recommended investigation for the suspected-narcolepsy indication, a clear mismatch that forces appropriateness to usually-not-appropriate and the recommendation to query-referrer regardless of completeness; suspected-narcolepsy is not an OSA-pathway indication, so no Epworth/STOP-BANG score adjustment applies here, but the missing Epworth still costs completeness and raises its own flag; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-not-appropriate + low priority + routine + query-referrer, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: Excessive daytime sleepiness with episodes of cataplexy triggered by laughter — query narcolepsy.

triage.notes: Query whether MSLT with preceding polysomnography should be requested instead of 'other'.
